gate.centre: an arm is off-centre when |mean z| > 1.645 RMS z / sqrt(n)
gate.width: per arm, the 90% chi-squared interval of the root mean square of z over its 200 worlds: above 1 narrow, below 1 wide, containing 1 right; coverage reported beside it, never gated
gate.paired: big_days against share_05: a paired bootstrap (2,000 draws over the same worlds) of the difference of their RMS z
gate.next: in order: an arm off-centre: read the worlds; ties narrow, control right, big_days not narrow: break ties at random in the samples; big_days narrow, share_05 right, big_days minus share_05 above 0: resample whole days or draw m of n; big_days and share_05 narrow: a small-count correction; control right with its upper end below 1.16 and no arm narrow: read the replica's seeds; control right with its upper end at 1.16 or above: inconclusive, more worlds; otherwise read the worlds
gate.limit: a tie is broken by row order; the worlds' rows are in random order and tied rows share their chance, so the ties arm can hardly show a tie effect and does not clear the replica, whose holdout is in time order

world.chances: logistic of a normal (mean -1.5, sd 1.0): about 21% cases, as the replica

objective: On invented worlds with known chances, is the decision core's day by day interval narrow, and is it the ties among a day's rows or the extremity of a day's best that makes it so?
